findings.issue: dedupeKey's prefix regex /^[a-z]{1,2}-?\d+(?:-\d+)*\s*:\s*/ strips more than the question ids the comment at lines 210-213 promises (Q3, RQ-12, F-1-001). After lowercasing, ordinary technical tokens such as ES2015, H2, V8, S3 or IE11 match too. Two distinct proposals like 'ES2015: what changed in module loading?' and 'ES2022: what changed in module loading?' get the same key, and admission prunes the second as 'dedupe', so a legitimate sub-question is silently lost. The test at frontier-admit.vitest.ts:332-337 pins only 'Q3', 'F-1-001' and 'We 2'. Reach: question text is free model-written text the contract allows, but the trigger is narrow and the loss is one optional frontier node, so P2. Fix: narrow the prefix to the run's real id shapes (for example q, rq or f followed by digits) and add the ES2015/ES2022 pair to the test.

findings.issue: The comment claims admission 'can only prune' a proposal under a closed node, but checkProposal (lines 525-527) prunes only a child of a missing or pruned parent. A child of a node closed as answered, blocked, exhausted or abstained passes every check and is admitted open. In the documented order (step_frontier_admit runs before step_reduce_state, and the reducer writes 'answered' during reduce at reduce-state.cjs:2017 and deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2455), no legitimate proposal targets an already-settled parent. So the code is acceptable and the comment overstates the guard. Reword it so a later reader does not rely on a prune that does not exist.

findings.issue: readProposalRows swallows a JSON.parse error with an empty catch and no comment. A torn frontier_proposal line in the leaf's delta is dropped with exit 0: nothing goes to stderr, and no pruned row is written to the store, so nobody can tell the proposal existed. floor.silent-failures (code-quality-standards.md:115) asks that an exception reach the caller or be logged with context. readNodeStore tolerates the same failure but states why (line 260), and readKnownTexts fails closed on bad input. P2 rather than the floor's default P1: the only loss is an optional proposal, and skipping the line is consistent with the module's own torn-line tolerance. Fix: count the skipped lines and write one stderr line, such as '[frontier-admit] skipped N unparsable delta lines', or at least state the reason in a comment.

findings.issue: The new CLI's fail-closed paths have no test. These include exit 2 with '--known-texts must hold a JSON array' (frontier-admit.cjs:991), the non-array seed input (line 997), an unknown command (line 1031), a missing flag value (line 955) and the exit-2 envelope in main (lines 1094-1096). The two suites spawn the CLI only on success paths (frontier-admit.vitest.ts:471, 638, 706 and frontier-admit-review.vitest.ts:386), and no test under runtime/tests mentions known-texts. The lens asks for a test for each changed behavior, and the code comments call these errors deliberate fail-closed choices ('A malformed known-texts file would silently widen admission'). A regression that made them fail open would pass the suite. Fix: add one spawnSync case that passes '{}' as --known-texts and asserts status 2 and the stderr message, plus one for an unknown command.
